beats.intro: Chapter forty-three. [[sub]]A compound event is made of two or more events happening together.
beats.compound: Flip a coin and roll a number cube. [[grid]]Every pair of results is one outcome: the coin's two sides, times the cube's six faces, makes twelve equally likely outcomes. [[ev]]The compound event tails and a three is just one of them. [[p]]So its probability is one twelfth.
beats.multiply: There's a faster way. [[sq]]Picture all the outcomes as one square of area one. [[col]]Rolling a three takes one sixth of the width. [[row]]Getting tails takes one half of the height. [[both]]Both happen only where the strips overlap: one half of one sixth, [[eq]]which is one twelfth. [[ind]]This works because the events are independent: the coin has no effect on the cube. [[rule]]For independent events, the probability of A and B is the probability of A times the probability of B.
beats.dep: Now a bag of ten marbles: four red and six blue. [[first]]Pick one without looking. The chance it's red is four tenths. [[keep]]Keep that marble out of the bag. [[now]]Now only nine marbles are left, and six of them are blue. [[second]]So the chance the second marble is blue is six ninths. [[dep]]The first pick changed the bag, so these events are dependent. [[mult]]Multiply the first probability by the second one, after the first event: four tenths times six ninths is twenty-four ninetieths, [[simp]]or four fifteenths.
beats.replace: Compare that with putting the marble back. [[back]]With replacement, the bag is the same for the second pick: [[ten]]six blue out of ten. [[ind]]The picks are independent, and the probability is four tenths times six tenths. [[diff]]Without replacement, the second fraction changes: both the top and the bottom can shrink.
beats.q2: Quick check. Two picks without replacement.
beats.cards: A deck has fifty-two cards, [[aces]]and four of them are aces. [[first]]Draw one card: the chance of an ace is four out of fifty-two. [[out]]Keep it out. [[left]]Now fifty-one cards are left, and only three are aces. [[mult]]So the probability of an ace, then another ace, is four fifty-seconds times three fifty-firsts, [[simp]]which is one out of two hundred twenty-one. That's less than half of one percent.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]A compound event combines two or more events. [[w2]]If the events are independent, multiply their probabilities. [[w3]]If the first event changes the second, they're dependent: multiply by the second probability after the first event has happened. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.finish: Nice work. That's the end of chapter forty-three, compound events.
